name: Chicken à la king
summary: Tender chicken, mushrooms and sweet peppers in a mild, velvety white sauce, spooned over rice for a weeknight dinner in half an hour.
about: The dish is usually credited to an American hotel kitchen in the early 1900s, but in South Africa it became a family standard, made on weeknights and for church and school functions, always with white rice.
steps: Put the rice on to cook (about 20 minutes) so it is ready with the sauce. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken, stirring, until white all over and just cooked through, 6 to 7 minutes. Tip it onto a plate.

Melt the butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add the onion, mushrooms and both peppers and fry, stirring, until the onion is soft and the mushrooms have released and lost their liquid, about 6 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute so it cooks and coats everything.

Pour in the stock a little at a time, stirring all the time so no lumps form, then stir in the milk. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pan with the peas and simmer for 3 more minutes, until the peas are bright green and the chicken is hot. Season with salt and pepper.
Dust with paprika and serve straight away over hot white rice.
